theorem: Let M be a finite-index g-stable divisor lattice in a K3 Picard lattice N, and let C be the full-dimensional pointed fixed section of a complete M-root chamber.  Assuming the displayed old facets are genuine N-roots and no N-root is orthogonal to the fixed space, C is the fixed section of an N-Weyl chamber if and only if no N-root hyperplane meets the relative interior of C.  For a finitely generated polyhedral C this is equivalent to every N-root restriction having one weak sign, but not vanishing identically, on all extreme rays.  The unique admissible H10/16 saturation and all ten admissible H10/45 overextensions fail by explicit (-2)-root cuts; the full-rank H11/29 carrier fails because twelve genuine facets have primitive ambient square -4 normals.
